newsitem.title: UK: Late bond market prices-Bunds take Treasury cue.
newsitem.headline: Late bond market prices-Bunds take Treasury cue.

text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.
GERMANY - German Bunds and futures received a modest lift from stronger U.S. Treasuries near the end of trading, but overall the session was characterised by nervous range-trading.
The September Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 110.87, up 0.17 from Monday's settlement price.
BRITAIN - UK gilt futures ended a touch easier but were fully recovered from their mid-morning lows as fresh demand emerged.
The September long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 113-18/32, up 1/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures traded in a narrow range on Tuesday in a tense but relatively quiet session, dominated by speculation about the impact on monetary union of French calls for time to reflect on the stability pact, designed to keep spending of euro members under control.
The June bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 129.46, down 0.10. from Monday's settlement price.
ITALY - Italian debt markets twitched up into positive territory at the close but traders said this was on short covering in a highly-strung market.

Confusion and nervousness over where European monetary union is heading has rendered the Btp market thin and flighty as investors opt to deal only when the herd does in order to be sure of liquidity. Otherwise they're keeping out.
The September bond future on LIFFE was trading at 129.88 up 0.41 from Monday's settlement price.
UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries opened firm, aided by a little short-covering after Monday's decline, analysts said.

The calendar of economic data due during the trading session includes no official government reports. The September Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-30/32, up 11/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.8 percent.
JAPAN - Key September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures closed Tuesday slightly easier after shedding earlier gains from weaker-than-expected April machinery orders data.

Japan's private-sector machinery orders, excluding those for machinery at electric power firms and for ships, showed a rise of a seasonally adjusted 7.2 percent in April from the previous month, which compared with economists' forecast of a rise of more than 10 percent. In after hours trading the September future on LIFFE was trading at 123.20, up 0.02 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
EUROBONDS - LONDON - The primary Eurobond market saw a steady flow of new issues, with dollars and marks the main currencies tapped.
Venezuela launched a well-flagged $315 million 10-year bond via ING Barings, which will be priced later to yield between 265 and 270 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes.
